mainTopic: Breaches in the walls of a מבוי (side vs. front, the crooked alley, wall remnants), and whether a רשות הרבים can be fixed with an עירוב.
overview: The amud opens with the end of a ruling: a breach in the side of a מבוי is allowed up to ten אמות, but a breach at its front only up to four טפחים. The גמרא asks why the front breach is not also treated as a doorway (פתחא). רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע answers that the front breach is in a corner, and people do not build doorways in corners. רב הונא disagrees and holds that every breach is limited to four טפחים. He cites רב's practical ruling in דמחריא, and רב נחמן בר יצחק adds a proof from רב's view that an L-shaped מבוי עקום is treated as open on both ends. רב חנן בר רבא rejects both proofs. דמחריא was a special local safeguard, and in the crooked alley crowds walk through the turn. The גמרא then reconciles רב הונא with רבי אמי and רבי אסי: their lenient case has wall remnants (גידודי) still standing. Finally a ברייתא teaches how to make an עירוב for a public thoroughfare. The גמרא begins to challenge it from a teaching of רבי יהודה, and that challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Side breach up to ten, front breach up to four
steps.stepSummary: A breach in the side of a מבוי is allowed up to ten אמות, but a breach at its front is allowed only up to four טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the מבוי is breached from its side, the limit is ten. If it is breached from its front, the limit is four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a rule about breaches in the walls of a מבוי, with different size limits for the side and for the front.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A breach in the side wall does not ruin the מבוי unless it reaches ten אמות. A breach at the front ruins it once it passes four טפחים, which is a much smaller gap. The rest of this passage asks why the two locations are treated so differently.

keyTerms.meaning: An alleyway with houses opening onto it, which can be fixed up so that carrying inside it is allowed
From its front or head (the end facing outward)

steps.confusionAlert: The two numbers use different units. The 'ten' means ten אמות, which is a large gap. The 'four' means four טפחים, which is only a few handbreadths. The difference between the two rules is much bigger than '10 vs 4' looks.

phrases.english: From its side — with ten (cubits);
from its front — with four (handbreadths).
phrases.notes: This is the end of a ruling whose attribution (רב חנין בר רבא in the name of רב) appears on the previous amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ruling of רב חנין בר רבא in the name of רב, which began at the end of the previous amud (5b).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A side breach invalidates the מבוי only at ten אמות. A front breach invalidates it already beyond four טפחים.

steps.title: Why not call the front breach a doorway too
steps.stepSummary: The side breach is allowed up to ten because it is viewed as a doorway. The גמרא asks why the front breach should not also be viewed as a doorway.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about the side, where the limit is ten? It is because we say it is a doorway. Then for the front too, let us say it is a doorway!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rule from step 1 by asking why the front and the side are treated differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to ten אמות, a gap counts as a normal doorway (פתחא), so it does not break the enclosure. That same reasoning seems to apply equally to a gap at the front. So the four-טפחים limit for the front looks unjustified.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? (a formula asking why two cases are treated differently)

phrases.english: What is different about the side, that the limit is ten —
because one says it is a doorway;
from the front too, let us say it is a doorway!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction made in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The four-טפחים limit for a front breach.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The doorway reasoning that allows ten אמות on the side should apply equally to the front.

steps.title: The front breach is in a corner, where no one builds doorways
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע explains that the case is a breach in a corner. People do not put doorways in corners, so the doorway reasoning does not apply there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: The case is one where it was breached at a corner, because people do not make a doorway in a corner.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא answers the challenge by narrowing the front case to a breach located in a corner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gap is treated as a doorway only if it looks like a place where people normally build doors. Nobody builds a doorway in a corner. So a corner gap cannot be called a פתחא, and the stricter four-טפחים limit applies to it.

keyTerms.meaning: People do not do (this); it is not normal practice

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a general principle: whether a gap counts as a doorway depends on what people normally build.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
For example, where it was breached at a corner,
for a doorway in a corner
people do not make.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ כְּגוֹן שֶׁנִּפְרַץ בְּקֶרֶן זָוִית
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case limitation (אוקימתא): the front case is set in a corner.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any front breach should count as a doorway, just like a side breach.
steps.terutzMaskana: The front case is a corner breach. A corner breach cannot be a doorway, so it is limited to four טפחים.

steps.title: רב הונא: both side and front are limited to four
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא disagrees with the distinction and holds that both a side breach and a front breach are allowed only up to four טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב הונא said: Both this and that are limited to four.
steps.whatsHappening: A different אמורא, רב הונא, gives his own competing opinion: no breach of more than four טפחים is allowed, wherever it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא rejects the side-versus-front distinction completely. In his view, the side breach gets the strict four-טפחים limit too. This makes the earlier question about doorways unnecessary for him.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, a student of רב

steps.confusionAlert: This רב הונא is a different person from רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע in step 3. The two disagree.

phrases.english: And Rav Huna said:
Both this and that are with four.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב הוּנָא אָמַר אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה בְּאַרְבָּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a dissenting opinion against the ruling in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any breach of more than four טפחים, whether on the side or at the front, invalidates the מבוי.

steps.title: רב הונא cites רב's practical ruling in דמחריא
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא tells רב חנן בר רבא not to argue with him, because רב himself ruled in practice according to רב הונא's view in דמחריא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so רב הונא said to רב חנן בר רבא: Do not disagree with me, for רב came to דמחריא and acted in practice according to my view.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא brings support for his opinion from a real ruling that רב issued in a place called דמחריא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling in step 1 was said in רב's name. רב הונא argues that רב's own behavior shows he was strict even about a side breach. A practical ruling (מעשה רב) is strong evidence of what a teacher really held.

keyTerms.meaning: Did a deed; issued a practical ruling

phrases.english: And so Rav Huna said to
Rav Chanan bar Rava:
Do not disagree with me,
for Rav arrived at Damcharya
and acted in practice according to me.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא לְרַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא לָא תִּפְלוֹג עִלַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב הונא's opinion from step 4.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's view that every breach is limited to four טפחים.

steps.title: Rejection: רב was adding a special safeguard
steps.stepSummary: רב חנן בר רבא answers that רב's ruling in דמחריא was a special stringency for a place that needed it, not the general law.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: רב found an open valley and fenced it in.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנן בר רבא pushes back on רב הונא's proof by explaining that רב's ruling was a one-time stringency for that place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The image is of an unguarded valley (בקעה) that gets a fence. רב saw that the people of דמחריא were lax and needed an extra safeguard, so he was strict with them. That local stringency does not show what the basic law is, so the original distinction between side and front stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Fenced it in; made a protective safeguard

steps.whatToRemember: There are two views. One says a side breach is allowed up to ten אמות, because it counts as a doorway, while a front (corner) breach is allowed only up to four טפחים. רב הונא says every breach is limited to four. רב הונא's proof from רב in דמחריא is rejected as a local safeguard.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches a key principle for learning from a מעשה: a ruling made to fix a special local problem cannot be used as proof of the general הלכה.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Rav found an open valley
and fenced it in with a fence.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב בִּקְעָה מָצָא וְגָדַר בָּהּ גָּדֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the ראיה brought in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from דמחריא is rejected; רב הונא's opinion itself is not disproven.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב's ruling was a special local stringency (a protective fence), not a statement of the basic law.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק supports רב הונא from the crooked-alley dispute
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says רב הונא's view makes more sense and points to a dispute between רב and שמואל about a מבוי עקום as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: The logic is on רב הונא's side. It was taught: about a crooked (L-shaped) alley, רב said it is treated like an alley open on both ends, and שמואל said it is treated like an alley closed on one end.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק sides with רב הונא and quotes an older argument between רב and שמואל that he will use as proof. This step only sets up the source. The actual proof comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מבוי עקום is an alley shaped like the letter L, opening to the street at both ends. From inside each arm, the turn into the other arm looks like an opening in the side wall at the corner. So this case can show how רב treats an opening on the side of a מבוי.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason like his view
As it was stated (introduces an אמוראים dispute)

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
It stands to reason like Rav Huna,
as it was stated: a crooked alleyway —
Rav said: its law is like an alley open on both ends.
phrases.notes: It needs the stricter treatment of an open-through alley.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: its law is like a closed alley.
phrases.notes: A side post or cross beam at each end is enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא מִסְתַּבְּרָא, דְּאִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב חנן בר רבא rejected the proof from דמחריא, a new proof for רב הונא is brought.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's view that a side breach in a מבוי is allowed only up to four טפחים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The dispute between רב and שמואל about a מבוי עקום, specifically רב's view that it is like מפולש

steps.title: What size opening is the crooked-alley dispute about
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case רב and שמואל are arguing about and rules out an opening wider than ten אמות, because שמואל would never call that closed.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with? If you say the opening at the turn is more than ten אמות wide, would שמואל really say it counts as closed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pins down the exact case of the רב and שמואל argument. It rules out the option of an opening wider than ten אמות, which prepares for the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An opening wider than ten אמות cannot be treated as a doorway by anyone. So it is impossible that שמואל would call such an alley closed. The argument must therefore be about an opening of ten אמות or less.

keyTerms.meaning: With what case are we dealing?
If you say (proposes an option, usually to reject it)
Would he say? (here a rhetorical 'surely not')

phrases.english: With what case are we dealing?
If you say it is more than ten (cubits) wide —
in such a case would Shmuel say its law is like a closed alley?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the case of the dispute quoted in step 7 so the proof can work.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How wide the opening at the turn of the מבוי עקום is in the dispute
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not more than ten אמות, since שמואל could not call that closed (completed in step 9)

steps.title: Even at ten, רב treats it as open, so a side breach is limited to four
steps.stepSummary: The case must be ten אמות or less. Since רב still treats it as open-through, it seems a side opening is not tolerated up to ten, which supports רב הונא's limit of four טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: So it must be a case of ten or less, and still רב said it is like an open-through alley. This shows that a breach in the side of a מבוי only works up to four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב נחמן בר יצחק's proof. Even when the side opening is ten or less, רב does not treat it as a doorway, which fits רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חנן בר רבא said a side breach is fine up to ten because it looks like a doorway. But at the turn of an L-shaped alley, רב treats even an opening of ten or less as breaking the alley. That matches רב הונא's rule that only up to four טפחים is allowed on the side.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not that... (introduces the forced conclusion)
A breach in the side of an alley

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the units. The 'ten' here is ten אמות (the width of the opening), while the 'four' is four טפחים, the much smaller limit רב הונא allows for a breach.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not about ten (or less),
and Rav said its law is like an open-through alley;
this shows a breach in the side of an alley is (limited to) four!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו בְּעֶשֶׂר, וְקָאָמַר רַב תּוֹרָתוֹ כִּמְפוּלָּשׁ, אַלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the case definition from step 8 to finish the proof begun in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's four-טפחים limit for a side breach
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's ruling that a מבוי עקום with a turn of ten אמות or less is מפולש

steps.title: רב חנן בר רבא: the crooked alley is different because the public walks through it
steps.stepSummary: רב חנן בר רבא rejects the proof. The L-shaped alley is a special case because many people pass through the turn, so it acts like a thoroughfare.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חנן בר רבא would say: it is different there, because many people cut through it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנן בר רבא defends his view by showing that the crooked-alley case does not prove a general rule about side breaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In an L-shaped alley the turn is the actual path people use to walk from one street to the other. Because there is real public traffic, רב is strict there. A normal side breach that people do not walk through can still be treated as a doorway up to ten.

keyTerms.meaning: Many people cut through it (public traffic)

steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs for רב הונא (דמחריא and the מבוי עקום) were rejected by רב חנן בר רבא as special cases. דמחריא was an extra stringency, and the crooked alley has public traffic. So his view that a side breach is allowed up to ten still stands.

phrases.english: And Rav Chanan bar Rava (would say):
It is different there,
because many people cut through it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא, שָׁאנֵי הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof completed in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the מבוי עקום, not רב's ruling itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The crooked alley has public foot traffic through the turn, which makes it different from an ordinary side breach

steps.title: רב הונא seems to contradict רבי אמי and רבי אסי
steps.stepSummary: After the last answer, the גמרא infers that רב הונא forbids a four-טפחים side breach even when crowds do not pass through it. It then asks how this differs from רבי אמי and רבי אסי, who allow a much larger gap.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we can learn that רב הונא holds that even if many people do not pass through the gap, it is still a problem. What is the difference between this and the ruling of רבי אמי and רבי אסי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the last answer to its logical end. It then points out that this result seems to clash with another ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 said רב's L-shaped alley case was special because crowds pass through it. That means רב הונא's four-טפחים limit has nothing to do with crowds, so even a quiet breach of more than four טפחים is a problem. But רבי אמי and רבי אסי said a board (פס) of four טפחים is enough to allow a gap of up to ten אמות. Why is a big gap fine for them, while a small gap is a problem for רב הונא?

keyTerms.meaning: By implication; 'we can learn from this that'
Pair of אמוראים who allowed a breach of up to ten אמות using a four-טפחים board

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a brand-new topic. It is a side effect of the previous answer (step 10). Once crowds are not the reason, רב הונא's limit looks very strict, and that strictness is what creates the clash.

phrases.english: By implication, Rav Huna holds
phrases.notes: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the answer in step 10.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא בָּקְעִי בַּהּ רַבִּים,
phrases.english: that even though many people do not pass through it [the breach still forbids carrying],

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא מִדְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי?
phrases.english: what is the difference from [the ruling of] Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi?
phrases.notes: They permitted a gap of up to ten אמות when a four-טפחים board stands there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the דחיה in step 10 and uses it to raise a contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's view that a side breach of more than four טפחים forbids carrying, even without crowds
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a small breach without crowds already forbids carrying, how can רבי אמי and רבי אסי permit a much larger gap of up to ten אמות?

steps.title: The difference is the leftover wall remnants
steps.stepSummary: In the case of רבי אמי and רבי אסי, pieces of the broken wall (גידודי) are still standing. In רב הונא's case they are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, there are remnants of the wall. Here, there are no remnants of the wall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by showing the two cases are physically different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where stumps of the old wall remain, they make the gap hard to walk through, so the wall still counts as basically standing. That is why רבי אמי and רבי אסי can allow a large gap. In רב הונא's case the breach is a clean, open gap, so even a small one of more than four טפחים breaks the enclosure.

keyTerms.meaning: Remnants or stumps of a wall that make passage hard

steps.whatToRemember: A breach with wall remnants still standing is treated more leniently than a clean, open breach. This is how רב הונא and רבי אמי/רבי אסי can both be right.

phrases.english: There, where there are wall remnants,
phrases.notes: Leftover pieces of the wall make it hard to pass through.

phrases.english: here, where there are no wall remnants.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases are simply gaps in a wall, so their rules should match.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wall remnants make the gap hard to pass through, which allows leniency. A clean gap gets no such leniency.

steps.title: A ברייתא: how to make an עירוב for a public thoroughfare
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a public road can be fixed with a צורת הפתח on one end and a לחי or קורה on the other. חנניה reports a dispute: בית שמאי require real, locking doors on both ends, while בית הלל require a door on one end and a לחי or קורה on the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our Rabbis taught: How do we make an עירוב for a public thoroughfare? One makes a doorway-frame on this side and a side post or crossbeam on that side. חנניה says: בית שמאי say one makes a door on this side and a door on that side, and when he goes out and comes in, he locks it. בית הלל say one makes a door on this side and a side post or crossbeam on that side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a ברייתא about fixing a public road so people can carry on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion says symbols are enough: a צורת הפתח on one end and a simple לחי or קורה on the other. חנניה says this is really a dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל. בית שמאי require actual doors on both ends that really get locked. בית הלל require a real door on one end, while the other end needs only a לחי or קורה.

keyTerms.meaning: We make an עירוב, so carrying is permitted
Form of a doorway: two posts with a beam across the top
Side post or crossbeam that marks an alley's opening

steps.confusionAlert: There are three positions here, not two. The unnamed first opinion needs a צורת הפתח on one end and a לחי or קורה on the other. בית הלל need a real door on one end and a לחי or קורה on the other. בית שמאי need real doors that lock on both ends.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is about to be challenged. The very idea of making an עירוב for a רשות הרבים will be questioned.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
How does one make an eruv for a public thoroughfare?
He makes a form of a doorway on this side,
and a side post or crossbeam on that side.
Chananya says:
Beit Shammai say:
He makes a door on this side and a door on that side,
and when he goes out and comes in, he locks [it].
phrases.notes: The door must really close, not just be symbolic.

phrases.english: Beit Hillel say:
He makes a door on this side,
and a side post or crossbeam on that side.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כֵּיצַד מְעָרְבִין דֶּרֶךְ רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: fixing a public thoroughfare, rather than a breach in an alley.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A public thoroughfare may be fixed with a צורת הפתח on one end and a לחי or קורה on the other. Per חנניה, בית שמאי require locking doors on both ends, and בית הלל require a door on one end and a לחי or קורה on the other.

steps.title: Can a public domain be fixed with an עירוב at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the whole idea of the ברייתא. It begins quoting a teaching of רבי יהודה that seems to say a רשות הרבים cannot be fixed this way.
steps.simpleTranslation: But can a public domain be fixed with an עירוב?! Wasn't it taught: Furthermore, רבי יהודה said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's basic assumption and starts quoting a source against it. The quote continues on the next amud, so this step is setting up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A true רשות הרבים is the strictest kind of public space. The גמרא doubts that a few doorway-frames or posts could turn it into a private area. It brings a ברייתא of רבי יהודה as evidence, but the content of that ברייתא comes only in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: Public domain, where carrying on שבת is forbidden מדאורייתא
Can it be fixed with an עירוב? (a challenging question)
But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא? (introduces a contradicting source)

phrases.english: But can a public domain be fixed with an eruv?!
But wasn't it taught:

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵר עַל כֵּן אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: Furthermore, Rabbi Yehuda said,
phrases.notes: The quotation continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the basic assumption of the ברייתא quoted in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's assumption that a רשות הרבים can be fixed with an עירוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא of רבי יהודה (completed on the next amud) apparently teaches that a רשות הרבים cannot be fixed this way.
